elements.description: The message box of an AI chat: model picker, voice input, attachments, connecting apps and requesting approval.

properties.name: hideConnectApps
properties.description: Leave out "Connect apps"; "Select a project" (unless hidden too) is offered straight away

properties.name: hideProject
properties.description: Leave out "Select a project"; once apps are connected the row folds away

properties.name: hideApproval
properties.description: Leave out "Request approval"

properties.name: placeholder
properties.description: Placeholder of the message field

properties.name: value
properties.description: The message

properties.name: models
properties.default: [ { id: "auto", name: "Auto", description: "Picks the best model for each task" }, { id: "claude", name: "Claude", description: "Thoughtful writing and code" }, { id: "chatgpt", name: "ChatGPT", description: "Quick answers for everyday tasks" }, ]
properties.description: Models in the picker; the first one is selected by default. An empty list disables the picker

properties.name: model
properties.description: Id of the selected model – unset, or one that's no longer in the list, selects the first

properties.name: loadMs
properties.description: How long "Connect apps" and "Request approval" load at least, in ms

properties.name: dictation
properties.default: "Draft a short update for the team about this week's progress"
properties.description: Sample transcript that appears word by word while recording when there's no onDictate

properties.name: demo
properties.description: Demo mode: connecting apps, requesting approval and dictation are simulated silently where their handlers are missing

properties.name: onDictate
properties.description:
Live speech-to-text for the mic, called when recording starts. Push the transcript so far with `onTranscript`
(and the input level, 0–1, with `onLevel` for the trace); stop listening when `signal` aborts – on Discard,
Use recording or removal. A rejection ends the recording with an error. Without it a sample transcript plays

properties.name: onSend
properties.type: ((message: string, details: ChatSendDetails) => void | Promise<unknown>) | undefined
properties.description:
Sends the message. Return a promise to keep the message (and a pending send button) until it settles: it is
cleared when it resolves and kept, with an error, when it rejects. `details` has the model, and the skill and its
arguments when the message starts with one

properties.name: onConnectApps
properties.description: Connects the user's apps; "Connect apps" keeps loading until a returned promise settles. Without it connecting is simulated

properties.name: onRequestApproval
properties.description: Requests unrestricted access – resolves, rejects and is simulated like onConnectApps

properties.name: mentions
properties.description: Opt-in: the / and @ picker on the message (tc-mention-picker). Its tc-pick bubbles from the composer

properties.name: skills
properties.description: Opt-in: the skills (slash commands) a message can start with – / at the start of a line opens them

properties.name: recentSkills
properties.description:
Ids of the skills used last, most recent first – listed first before anything is typed. Unset, the composer
remembers the picks made in it

properties.name: searchSkills
properties.description: Finds skills on the app's side in place of the built-in filter over `skills` (see ChatSkillSearch)

properties.name: skill
properties.description: Id of the message's skill ("" for none). Setting it puts that skill's token at the start of the message

properties.name: hideSkillsButton
properties.description: Leave out the "/" button that opens the skills list

properties.name: skillsPlaceholder
properties.description: The empty message's placeholder while skills are on – default: the placeholder plus "/ for skills"

properties.name: context
properties.description:
Opt-in: what's in context, as chips above the composer (tc-context-tray). Changes come as tc-items-change; the
composer keeps the new list unless a listener prevents it

properties.name: contextLimit
properties.description: The context window the tray measures against, in tokens

properties.name: modelSwitcher
properties.description: Where the model switch is: in the card (the default), or in the toolbar row as tc-model-picker's menu

properties.name: settings
properties.description: Opt-in: the model settings (by parameter id), edited in a popover from the toolbar. Changes come as tc-settings-change

properties.name: settingsModel
properties.description: The model the settings are for – only the parameters it supports are shown; unset shows them all

properties.name: prompts
properties.description: Opt-in: saved prompts, in a popover from the toolbar. A used prompt goes in at the caret (tc-prompt-pick)

properties.name: pageContext
properties.description: Opt-in: what's on the page, as a chip in the toolbar that connects or disconnects it (tc-page-context-change)

properties.name: disclaimer
properties.description: One quiet line under the composer, e.g. "AI can make mistakes. Check important info." – it also describes the message field

properties.name: pickedSkill
properties.description: The message's skill, from its id – a skill the composer hasn't seen is named by its id

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-value-change
events.description: The message changed (`{ value: string }`) – typing, dictation, clearing after a send; cancelable – prevent it to keep `value` (controlled use)

events.name: tc-model-change
events.description: A model was picked in the menu (`{ model: string; choice: ChatModel }`); cancelable

events.name: tc-send
events.description: A message was sent (`ChatSend`: `{ message, model, skill, args }` – `skill` is the picked skill's `{ id, name }` or null, `args` the text after its token); `onSend` may return a promise to keep it until it settles

events.name: tc-skill-change
events.description: The message's skill changed (`ChatSkillChange`: `{ skill, previous, reason }`); cancelable when it was picked, replaced or removed – prevent it to keep the message as it is

events.name: tc-attach
events.description: The plus button was pressed – open your own file or folder picker here

events.name: tc-connect-apps
events.description: "Connect apps" was pressed; `onConnectApps` may return a promise it waits for

events.name: tc-request-approval
events.description: "Request approval" was pressed; `onRequestApproval` may return a promise it waits for

events.name: tc-settings-change
events.description: The model settings changed in the settings popover (`ChatSettingsChange`: `{ value, changed }`); cancelable – prevent it to control `settings`

events.name: tc-prompt-pick
events.description: A prompt was picked in the prompt library (`ChatPromptPick`: `{ prompt, template, values }`); cancelable – prevent it to place the prompt yourself

events.name: tc-page-context-change
events.description: The page context chip was toggled, or an attached item removed (`ChatPageContextChange`: `{ pageContext, change }`); cancelable – prevent it to control `pageContext`

functions.name: defaultChatModels
functions.description: The models the composer offers when none are given

changelog: **Skills in `tc-chat-composer`:** `skills`, `recentSkills`, `searchSkills`, `skill`. - **Typeahead:** typing `/` at the start of a message opens a ranked typeahead, grouped by source, with recent skills first. - **Token:** a pick adds a tinted `/skill` token with its argument hint. - **Events:** `tc-send` gains `skill` and `args`, and there is a new `tc-skill-change`. - **Toolbar:** an optional "/" button.
**`tc-chat-composer` toolbar:** - model picker, settings and prompt library; - page context you can connect and disconnect; - a disclaimer line under the input; - `hide*` props for each piece.

chat-composer (the Lit element and `trenchcoat/react`): opt-in `mentions` (a `tc-mention-picker` on the message) and `context` / `context-limit` (a `tc-context-tray` above it). Without them it renders as before.

features.name: light-dark()
features.why: Every colour token is a light / dark pair; without it no colour token resolves.

features.name: Form association (ElementInternals)
features.why: The element's value is submitted with its form, and it takes part in form validation and reset.

features.name: color-mix()
features.why: Tints and washes mixed from the tokens.

features.name: Container query units (cqi, cqw…)
features.why: Sizes relative to the component's own width.

features.name: Container size queries
features.why: Components adapt to the width they're given, not the window's.

features.name: inert
features.why: Closed and leaving parts are out of the tab order and hidden from screen readers.

features.name: :has()
features.why: Layout and state that depend on what's inside a part (an icon present, a focused field).

features.name: :is() and :where()
features.why: Every rule is keyed on :where() so the page can override it.

features.name: scrollbar-width
features.without: Scrollbars keep the browser's default width.

features.name: Popover API
features.without: Lists open fixed to the window instead of in the top layer, so a clipping ancestor or a modal can cover them.

features.name: @property
features.without: The registered custom properties don't interpolate, so the transitions and spins they drive jump to their end state.

features.name: adoptedStyleSheets
features.without: Each element type's CSS goes into one <style> element in <head> instead – it looks and works the same.

features.name: forced-colors media query
features.without: In a forced-colours mode the browser's own adjustments apply, without the components' fixes.

features.name: overscroll-behavior: contain
features.without: Scrolling past the end of a list carries on scrolling the page.
